Conversions between model representations

Source: R/transfer-functions.R
ctrl_tf2ss.Rd

  • ctrl_zpk2tf() and ctrl_tf2zpk() convert between zero-pole-gain and polynomial forms (SISO).

  • ctrl_tf2ss() realizes a proper transfer function in state space. SISO models use the controllable canonical form. MIMO models are realized element by element and then reduced with ctrl_minreal() when minimal = TRUE.

  • ctrl_ss2tf() computes each SISO channel's transfer function. With minimal = TRUE (default) each channel is first reduced to a minimal realization, so uncontrollable or unobservable modes do not appear as canceling pole-zero pairs. The numerator of channel \((i,j)\) is computed from the identity \(c (sI - A)^{-1} b = [\det(sI - A + bc) - \det(sI - A)] / \det(sI - A)\).

Usage

ctrl_tf2ss(sys, minimal = TRUE, tol = NULL)

ctrl_ss2tf(sys, minimal = TRUE, tol = NULL)

ctrl_zpk2tf(sys)

ctrl_tf2zpk(sys)

Arguments

sys

A model.

minimal

Reduce to a minimal realization (see details).

tol

Tolerance passed to ctrl_minreal().

Value

The converted model.

Details

Root finding and characteristic polynomials are ill-conditioned for high-order models; prefer state-space computations for large systems.

Examples

G <- ctrl_tf(c(1, 2), c(1, 3, 2))
ss <- ctrl_tf2ss(G)
ss
#> State-space model (continuous time)
#> 1 states, 1 inputs, 1 outputs
#> 
#> A =
#>    x1
#> x1 -1
#> 
#> B =
#>        u1
#> x1 0.4472
#> 
#> C =
#>       x1
#> y1 2.236
#> 
#> D =
#>    u1
#> y1  0
ctrl_ss2tf(ss)
#> Transfer function (continuous time)
#> 
#>         1
#>   ---------
#>   s +     1
ctrl_tf2zpk(G)
#> Zero-pole-gain model (continuous time)
#>   gain: 1
#>   zeros: -2+0i
#>   poles: -2+0i, -1+0i
